enunciado: A palavra "their", na expressão "their equipment", indica posse.
O pronome "they" é um pronome pessoal do caso oblíquo (objeto).
The connector "therefore" (second paragraph) introduces a contrast with what was said before.
In the second paragraph, the word "their", in "lose their habitats", refers to "wild animals".
The connector "For this reason" (third paragraph) introduces a consequence of the difficulty of fighting fires.
comentario: Por isso, prevenção e detecção precoce.

enunciado: The connector "However" (second paragraph) introduces an idea that adds an example to the previous paragraph, without any contrast.
comentario: "However" introduz **contraste**: first aid não é só para situações dramáticas.

enunciado: The pronoun "This" (second paragraph, "This allows operators...") refers to the fact that operators can see the location of every unit.
The connector "Still" (third paragraph) introduces an idea that contrasts with the advantages mentioned before.
In the last sentence, the pronoun "themselves" refers to "others".
The connector "but", in "but must also listen" (third paragraph), introduces a contrast.
The expression "instead of" (second paragraph) introduces an alternative to fighting the current.
comentario: Em vez de lutar, nadar paralelo.

enunciado: In the second paragraph, the question "What motivates these people, then?" is used to introduce an explanation of the volunteers' reasons.
The connector "Still" (fourth paragraph) introduces an addition to the positive aspects mentioned before, reinforcing them.
The connector "however" (second paragraph) introduces a conclusion drawn from the previous idea.
The connector "because" (second paragraph) introduces a reason for the previous statement.
The connector "instead" (second paragraph) introduces an alternative to the idea previously rejected.
comentario: Não vão sumir; em vez disso, serão remodeladas.

enunciado: The connector "however" (second paragraph) introduces a contrast with the previous statement.
The expression "in other words" introduces a contradiction of the idea previously presented.
The term "the tropical landscape" (second paragraph) refers to the Amazon rainforest.
In the last sentence of the second paragraph, the pronoun "they" refers to "some portions of the tropical landscape".
comentario: Gabarito: CERTO. Release more carbon than they store.

enunciado: The words "however" and "but" (last paragraph) are both used to introduce a statement that contrasts with something that has been said before.
The connectors "however", "nevertheless" and "although" express addition.
The connectors "moreover", "furthermore" and "in addition" express contrast.
The connectors "therefore", "thus" and "consequently" express cause.
The connectors "because", "since" and "due to" express contrast.
The connector "although" expresses cause, being equivalent to "because".
In "Although it was raining, the team continued the search", the connector "although" introduces a concession.
The expressions "for example", "for instance" and "such as" introduce conclusions.
The connector "unless", in "Do not enter unless you are wearing protective gear", means "if not".
The connector "whereas" introduces an addition, being equivalent to "and also".
In "Despite the strong winds, the fire was controlled", "despite" expresses contrast, being followed by a noun phrase.
The connector "so", in "It was dangerous, so they waited for backup", introduces a contrast.
The connector "while" can express contrast, as in "Some workers fear losing their jobs, while others see new opportunities".
In "The firefighter helped the woman and her son", the possessive "her" refers to the firefighter.
In "The volunteers left their homes", the possessive "their" refers to "homes".
The relative pronoun "which" is used for people, and "who" is used for things.
In "The officer whose team won the competition was promoted", "whose" indicates possession.
In "The equipment which they bought is new", the relative pronoun "which" refers to "they".
The pronoun "it", in "The fire spread quickly; it destroyed three houses", refers to "three houses".
The demonstrative "these" is used with plural nouns that are near the speaker, while "those" refers to plural nouns that are farther away.
The object pronoun corresponding to "we" is "our", as in "They helped our".
In "She hurt herself during training", the reflexive pronoun "herself" refers to someone other than "she".
comentario: O reflexivo retoma o **próprio sujeito** (ela se machucou).

enunciado: The connector "on the other hand" introduces a contrasting point of view.
The connector "as a result" introduces a cause of what was mentioned before.
The connector "besides" can introduce an additional piece of information.
In "Firefighters, whose work is dangerous, must train constantly", the clause between commas adds extra information about firefighters in general.
The connector "yet", in "The job is hard, yet rewarding", expresses addition.
In "Lifeguards advise swimmers to stay calm. This is the best way to survive a rip current", the word "This" refers to staying calm.
The connector "in order to", as in "They trained hard in order to pass the test", expresses purpose.
The connector "thus" introduces a contrast and could be replaced by "but".
